name: White-fronted Ground-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Andes of southern peru (ancash) to western bolivia and far northern chile
description: Largest ground-tyrant, usually identified readily by (relatively) big size and high Andean range. Usually seen as singles or pairs foraging on bogs, but also ranges into adjacent rocky puna habitats.

name: Bahia Antwren
rangeDescription: Coastal eastern brazil (bahia south of salvador)
description: Small, long-tailed antwren. Males resemble many other antwrens, mostly gray with a black cap, a long white eyebrow, and a black eye-stripe.

name: Bonaparte's Nightjar
rangeDescription: Lowlands of sumatra, belitung (off southeastern sumatra), and borneo
description: Small dark-brown nightjar of lowland forests. Bright white bib often noticeable.

name: Great Hornbill
rangeDescription: Lowlands of india to southwestern china, southeastern asia, and sumatra
description: A huge, distinctive hornbill with a large yellow bill and casque. Black face, wings, and breast contrast with white neck, belly, and tail.

name: Patagonian Forest Earthcreeper
rangeDescription: Central chile and southwestern argentina
description: Rather local breeder in drier Patagonian areas with open forest and shrubby slopes. Migrates across the Andes to winter in Chile, where it is found in matorral and other shrubby habitats.

name: Ochre-collared Monarch
rangeDescription: Lowlands of northern new guinea, including yapen (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: A slender, medium-sized bird of lowland and foothill forest. Fairly long tail and black face with gray bill and blue eye wattle.

name: Orange Bullfinch
rangeDescription: Montane forest of northern pakistan to northwestern india (himachal pradesh)
description: A small, brightly colored bullfinch. The male is orange with black mask, wings, and tail.

name: Great Knot
rangeDescription: Northeastern siberia; winters to india, southeastern asia, philippines, and australia
description: Medium-sized, stocky shorebird found almost exclusively on coastal mudflats during migration, seldom inland. Distinctive adult in breeding plumage has a brick-orange upperwing patch, blackish back, and chest with black mottling.

name: Hudson's Canastero
rangeDescription: Far southern brazil to uruguay and eastern argentina (south to río negro)
description: Distinctive, heavily streaked ovenbird with a long spiky tail. Note the thin black streaks on the flanks.

name: Whistling Kite
rangeDescription: Australia, new guinea, and new caledonia
description: Large sandy-colored raptor. In flight it has a strong underwing pattern, and holds its wings in a bent M-shape.

name: Brown-bellied Stipplethroat
rangeDescription: Eastern venezuela to the guianas and northeastern amazonian brazil
description: Tiny bird; forages actively, probing into dead leaves suspended in vegetation. Note small size, overall brownish coloration, and pale eyes.

name: Gray-fronted Quail-Dove
rangeDescription: Cuba (rare)
description: A multicolored chunky dove of dense, wet forests with thick leaf-litter. It is most often found on the ground, sometimes in association with Blue-headed or Ruddy Quail-Doves.

name: Red-knobbed Coot
rangeDescription: Southern spain and morocco; eastern and southern africa and madagascar
description: Mostly sooty gray waterbird with a white beak and frontal shield. Breeding adults have two small reddish horns, but at other times difficult to separate from Eurasian Coot.

name: Swift Parrot
rangeDescription: Tasmania and flinders island; winters eastern and southeastern australia
description: Colorful migratory parrot with long red pointed tail. Breeds in Tasmania and migrates to southeastern Australia in autumn and winter.

name: White-browed Hermit
rangeDescription: Foothills of southeastern peru to central bolivia
description: Small, orangey hermit of Andean foothills. Orange below, with a black mask, white eyebrow, and green back.

name: Delta Amacuro Softtail
rangeDescription: Northeastern venezuela (southern portion of the río orinoco delta)
description: Distinctive streaky brown bird of riverine habitats of the Orinoco Delta. Most of body brown with buffy streaks (tear-shaped on underparts).

name: Mouse-brown Sunbird
rangeDescription: Southern senegal to cameroon, gabon, northern angola, and southwestern democratic republic of the congo
description: A sunbird that is closely tied to water, most often encountered in mangroves, farmlands, and along large rivers as far inland as Mali. Gray-brown above and dingy gray-white below with distinctive bright white spectacles and a relatively large, short bill without much of a curve.

name: Bronze-winged Jacana
rangeDescription: Lowlands of india to southwestern china, southeastern asia, sumatra, and java
description: Gangly inhabitant of well-vegetated wetlands, especially ponds and lakes with floating vegetation. Adult’s dark neck and bright white eyebrows are unmistakable.

name: Chinese Fulvetta
rangeDescription: Mountains of south-central china (southwestern gansu to southeastern qinghai, sichuan, and northwestern yunnan)
description: Dull brown fulvetta with pale eyes, found only in central and south-central China. Note streaky throat, dark lores, and pale, narrow wing panel.

name: Miombo Scrub-Robin
rangeDescription: Angola to democratic republic of the congo, burundi, zambia, southwestern tanzania, and northern mozambique
description: Pretty robin with a brown back, boldly marked face, and unstreaked rufous chest. Found in miombo broadleaf woodland.
